precepts.text: Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. That is what a man in his truth is going to do. He is going to give his life. That is his time. That is his patience. That is his problems. That is his traumas. You sisters as well, you are going to give your lives for that. Everything should revolve around being an Israelite. I had a conversation with a brother and he was asking me how he normalizes the lifestyle of an Israelite. And the question itself was the answer. Normalize that in your everyday life. When you wake up in the morning, you are an Israelite. You are not a black man in America. That is just what you have been labeled as. So the same way that you grew up and were admonished in media with being a negro in America, you have got to reverse that and admonish yourself in what an Israelite is, the Israelite culture. You have got to put yourself in those shoes at every given moment. Your thought process has to be an Israelite man, not a man in America. And call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time. That is how you are going to normalize what it is to be an Israelite, a person that is keeping God's commandments. So shall ye receive great honour and an everlasting name. That is how we are going to receive that name. That is how we are going to break those generational curses that we have been stigmatized to.
precepts.point: So now we see, okay, I see the mistake that they made. I am not going to make that same mistake. I am going to be better than the men before me, to the best of my ability, with the spirit that the Lord gave me.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

precepts.why:
The Bible has given us all the instructions we need to fix ourselves, and the ultimate fix to all of our problems is remembering and keeping the laws of God. Mattathias told his sons: “Now therefore, my sons, be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.”

That is what a man in his truth is going to do: give his life. That is his time, his patience, his problems, his traumas. Sisters as well, you are going to give your lives for that. Everything should revolve around being an Israelite.

A brother asked how he could normalize the lifestyle of an Israelite, and the question itself was the answer: normalize it in your everyday life. When you wake up in the morning, you are an Israelite. You are not a black man in America; that is just what you have been labeled. The same way you grew up admonished by the media in being a negro in America, you have to reverse that and admonish yourself in what an Israelite is, the Israelite culture. Your thought process has to be an Israelite man, not a man in America.

“Call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time”. That is Romans 15:4: the things written aforetime were written for our learning. Remembering the acts of our fathers is how you normalize what it is to be an Israelite, a person keeping God's commandments. We see where they overcame and where they were punished, and we say, I see the mistake they made, I am not going to make it; I am going to be better than the men before me.

“so shall ye receive great honour and an everlasting name”. That is how we receive that name, and how we break the generational curses we have been stigmatized with.

precepts.text: He likens his judgment unto a ring. A ring is like a circle: there is no slackness of the last, and no swiftness of the first. His judgments on the earth are a continual event that reoccurs over and over. That is why Paul said comfort yourselves through what is written in the testimonies of the past, because what you are living is a reoccurring event.
precepts.point: In order to deal with these reoccurring events, we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors from the past, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
Solomon said, “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” Paul says the same thing in different words: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”. Our learning today. There are no new incidents on this earth; everything that was done in the past is reoccurring.

Ezra shows it with a ring: “And he said unto me, I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is like a circle. “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first”. Slackness means slow: there is no slowness of the last judgments and no swiftness of the first. His judgments on the earth are a continual event that reoccurs over and over; it is the same thing.

That is why Paul said to comfort ourselves through what is written in the testimonies of the past: what we are living is a reoccurring event. To deal with these reoccurring events we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors, “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

We see it now. Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and gathered the rulers to its dedication, setting up a one world religion; today pastors gather to pray over and dedicate a towering gold statue of Donald Trump. What we read in Daniel 3 is coming to pass again, because the judgments go around like a ring.

precepts.text: All the prophets spoke: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Hosea. He multiplied visions and used similitudes, or parables, by the ministry of the prophets, comparing one thing to another.
precepts.point: In order to deal with these reoccurring events, we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors from the past, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
The things written aforetime were written for our learning, and Hosea shows how they were written: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

All the prophets spoke: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, even Hosea. God multiplied visions, and he used similitudes, or parables, by the ministry of the prophets, comparing one thing to another.

That is how the scriptures teach us today. The past is a similitude of what is happening now, and by comparing one thing to another we can see our own time in what was written. The last beast of Revelation 13 is described with the leopard, the bear and the lion of Daniel 7: it carries the attributes of Greece, Persia and Media, and Babylon. The golden image of Daniel 3 stands again in our day.

So we read the prophets as similitudes, and through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope, because the Most High already showed in the past what he will do in the future.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning. After reading what Christ said, we are going back historically regarding brothers becoming betrayers.
precepts.point: And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. Christ prophesied brothers becoming betrayers; that is today's lesson.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Christ prophesied it: “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.” Brothers becoming betrayers. Paul shows where to look to understand it: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” So after reading what Christ said, we go back historically to what was written aforetime about brothers who became betrayers.

The history is in 2 Maccabees 3. The holy city was at peace “and the laws were kept very well, because of the godliness of Onias the high priest, and his hatred of wickedness.” Because of Onias' faith, his strength and love for God's laws, everybody else was inspired, and even the kings honoured the place and magnified the temple with their best gifts. That is the mentality we all must have: “Ye that love the Lord, hate evil.” You don't hate evil as long as you watch pornography at home.

“But one Simon of the tribe of Benjamin, who was made governor of the temple, fell out with the high priest about disorder in the city.” Onias had the last say; Simon did not agree. “And when he could not overcome Onias, he gat him to Apollonius”, governor of Celosyria and Phenice, up by Damascus. He ran to the other nations against his own brother, “And told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money.” You don't want to do what I say? I'm going to tell the other nations about all the money in the temple. You can't make this stuff up. That money was for the Levites, the strangers, the fatherless and the widows.

Ecclesiasticus names that kind of man: “there is a friend, which is only a friend in name. Is it not a grief unto death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?” He rejoices with you in prosperity, “but in the time of trouble will be against him.” It is the same with those who leave the truth today: “I hate the work of them that turn aside.” It was written for our learning, so that we can see the betrayer Christ spoke of coming and not be moved.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. When jail, affliction and tribulation come, you remember you read it, so you humble yourself to see what the Lord is showing you.
precepts.point: Get rid of your own personal demonic sin before you line a brother up for his failure. In the furnace every evil thought and secret act against the congregation comes back.

note.label: A Soul Without Purpose

precepts.why:
Christ told the apostles, “behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”, and he is telling us today these things are going to happen to us. How do we know? “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

You read the scripture say we are going to go to jail. You read that we are going to be afflicted, that tribulation is going to hit us. So wherever you find yourself, when these things happen you remember reading it, and you say, I cannot fight it, this is of the Lord. So you humble yourself to see what he is trying to show you.

That is why you cannot be a snake and think you are going to get away with it, selling your soul for nothing, for a little seventy dollars. The day you are sitting in the furnace of the fire, all of it comes back: the evil thoughts toward your brother, smiling in your brother's face while breaking bread, the things you did in secret against the congregation.

You have your own personal demonic sin you are fighting with. Get rid of that first before you think about lining a brother or a sister up for their failure. What was written aforetime was written so that when the trial comes, you have patience and hope, and you stand.

precepts.text: The Father of mercies and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble.
precepts.point: Through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope that a saviour is coming to redeem the children of Israel. 2 Corinthians 1 calls him the God of all comfort, who comforts us in tribulation so we can comfort our people, who are in trouble today, with this Bible: the straight and narrow, not the left or the right.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Where does that comfort come from? Paul says, “Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort”. The God of all comfort, and we find that comfort in this Bible.

“Who comforteth us in all our tribulation”. Christ comforts us in all our tribulations. The things written aforetime show the Israelites going into captivity after captivity and committing sin after sin, but they also show the redemption: when the Israelites came out of captivity, they had to keep the commandments. That is our comfort, and our hope is that a saviour is coming to redeem the children of Israel.

And he comforts us for a reason: “that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.” Are our people in trouble today? Absolutely. So what are we supposed to comfort our people with? This Bible.

We have to let our people know there is a better way. Go this way, not that way. Do not go to the left and do not go to the right. Go to this Bible, the straight and narrow path. The comfort the scriptures gave us is the comfort we carry to our people.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning. Learn them and apply them.
precepts.point: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge, that I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth? The Bible is God's excellent things, not a prosperity tool or a debate about what we feel like doing. He expects excellence, so change your mind to his standard instead of the crumbs society leaves our people.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The excellent things God wrote in Proverbs 22:20, the counsels and knowledge that make us “know the certainty of the words of truth”, were written for us to learn.

And not only to learn: “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These excellent things are written for us to apply to our lives, so that we can be excellent and great in God’s eyes. Learn and apply, that is what Romans 15:4 is telling us.

Everything in this Bible is the excellent things of God, the truth he wants us to know. It is not to be used to get rich off of prosperity teaching, and it is not up for debate for us to decide what we should and should not do. It is not up for debate whether we want to be great or average. God gave us excellent things because he expects excellence out of us.

So we have to change our mindset and live up to the standards of God, not the standards the world has placed on black men and women and Hispanic men, to be comfortable with the crumbs society gives us. Those excellent things are what we have to apply, and it starts with a change in the mind.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
precepts.point: Set thine house in order and reprove thy people. Order your own life first, then you can reprove others.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezra to “comfort such of them as be in trouble”, and that comfort comes out of the scriptures: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” That which was written was upright, and we have to understand it and follow it. That's the pattern.

That is where our hope comes from. When we look at the history of our forefathers, whatever they went through, brothers and sisters, is what we are going to go through, so we are not shocked at what is going on. And it is the same in the body: the Captain went through it, I can go through it; the Deacon went through it, I can go through it; the sister went through it, I can go through it. That is the comfort that keeps us from giving up.

So don't give up. No matter what, stand up. This profession, made before many witnesses, is all we have; some of us have twenty years and more in this truth. Where can we go? This is our life. Don't let Satan take it away from you, and don't give it up for Babylon's money; Babylon will destroy your soul. Set your house in order, revive your own soul first, and then revive your people.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
precepts.point: Solomon praised the dead more than the living; Job wished he had died from the womb. The comfort is in the scriptures.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power”. That's us. Our oppressors have power: they organize themselves, pass laws and policies, colonize, oppress and exploit. And the Israelites had no comforter.

So what is supposed to comfort us? Paul says: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Whatsoever was written aforetime means this Bible, and it was written for our learning. We ought to learn from what happened to the Israelites, to the apostles, and to Christ.

“comfort of the scriptures”: this is our comforter. The scriptures of this Bible are where the oppressed find comfort, and that is what we need to hope in.

The oppressors hold all the cards right now, and the one who has no comforter in the world has one in the word. If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, the nations would have swallowed us up; it is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed.

precepts.text: The things written aforetime were written for our learning; the history of Egypt teaches this captivity.
precepts.point: The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning, and the thing that hath been is that which shall be. That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon, and of the Greeks, because these things must come to pass.

note.label: Exodus 10: The Most High Hardens Pharaoh to Shew His Signs

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The hardening of Pharaoh's heart was written down for us. The history of Egypt teaches this captivity.

That is why so many similarities appear between the captivities: this captivity carries the marks of Egypt, of Babylon and of the Greeks. What the Most High did with Pharaoh, hardening him so he would not let Israel go, he does with the rulers of spiritual Egypt today. So we read Egypt to understand where we are, and we take hope from it: the Most High brought Israel out then, and he is in control now.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.
precepts.point: They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun, and these things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.

note.label: Numbers 11: Beware of Murmuring

precepts.why:
They had just seen the Lord consume the complainers in the uttermost parts of the camp, and they went back and did the same thing: they wept for what they ate freely in Egypt, right after the Lord destroyed the Egyptians to bring them out of bondage. We are the same people today; there is nothing new under the sun. It is the same now with the entertainments and comforts of this captivity, and some will do the same thing again in the wilderness when the Most High brings the people back out.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These things were written aforetime for our learning, so we can read them and refuse to do as they did.

precepts.text: Things written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
precepts.point: Let that be a lesson learned, for whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

note.label: Numbers 26: The Second Census of the Families of Israel

precepts.why:
A whole generation numbered at Sinai fell in the wilderness, and only Caleb and Joshua were left. Let that be a lesson learned.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The second census was written for our learning: follow fully like Caleb and zealously like Phinehas, and through patience and comfort of the scriptures have hope of entering the land.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning; the history shows where the shut heaven happened.
precepts.point: The things written aforetime were written for our learning: Jeremiah shows this curse landing in Israel's history, the ground chapt because there was no rain, and the confession that our backslidings are many.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The curse of the shut heaven was not written as a warning that never landed. It was written aforetime, and the history shows where it happened: Jeremiah records the ground chapt because there was no rain, and the confession that our backslidings are many.

So we go to the history for our learning. Moses said take heed that your heart be not deceived, lest the Lord shut up the heaven; Israel's own history shows the heaven shut. Reading what was written aforetime, we learn what turning aside to other gods brings, and through the scriptures we have hope.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
precepts.point: Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans Paul quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

That is “Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations” in the mouth of an apostle. We go to the scriptures, see how the Most High intervened and saved our forefathers, see where they went wrong, and take patience, comfort and hope from it. That is how you are supposed to read this Bible, like you stepped into the events themselves.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.
precepts.point: That is good history we read today about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of you may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring your children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from; use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

“Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground.” What does that mean? What Samuel said, it came to pass. And “all Israel from Dan even to Beer–sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the Lord.”

That is good history we read about Samuel; take heed to what you have heard, and do not let it slip. Some of us may be in these same situations: putting other people before God, honouring our children above God and not restraining them, or hearing the Lord call once, twice, three times without answering the call. This history is here for us to learn from. Use it, lest the judgments of God be passed upon us when he is angry, for whatever the Most High says, Christ follows, because that is the order: God, Christ, man, woman, children.

precepts.text: The things written beforetime were written for our learning, which is why Mordecai would not accept a weak answer from Esther but held her to her purpose.
precepts.point: So Mordecai went his way and did according to all Esther commanded him. She had her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people.

note.label: Esther 4: Mordecai Charges Esther for Such a Time as This

precepts.why:
“So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.” He would not accept a weak answer from her; he held her to her purpose until she answered, “if I perish, I perish.”

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” This is why the account is written: for our learning. Esther with her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people, and Mordecai holding her to it, are written so that we, through patience and the comfort of the scriptures, might have hope.

precepts.text: Whatsoever was written aforetime was written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope, even when men call us a hate group.
precepts.point: But Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him, so there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Eliphaz's answer to Job was written for our learning. Men throw our righteousness back at us as filthy rags, as if keeping the commandments profits nothing, and call us a hate group, the way Eliphaz asked Job, “Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous?”

Through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope, even when men call us a hate group: Christ told us if we keep the commandments and follow him, we will rule on thrones with him. So there is falsehood in Eliphaz's answer, and the scriptures give us the hope he tried to take from Job.

precepts.text: Things written before were written for our learning, sending us back to find the righteous path.
precepts.point: When brothers ask "were you there?" or "how you know what color he was?" the answer is that the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars, and they told the following generations. We are supposed to search the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What the fathers told, what the Most High did in the times of old, was written down for our learning. It sends us back to find the righteous path.

That is the answer to were you there and how you know what color he was: the fathers heard and witnessed the Red Sea and the wars and told the following generations, and it was written for us. We are supposed to search the scriptures, and through their patience and comfort we have hope.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” The history of our fathers tempting the Most High in the wilderness is one of those things written aforetime. It is not there for a story; it is there for our learning.

So when Psalm 95 brings up the provocation and the day of temptation in the wilderness, we take it the way Paul tells us to: learn from it, do not harden your mind to sin as they did, and through the patience and comfort of the scriptures have hope.

precepts.text: Whatever was written before was written for our learning, that we might have hope.

note.label: Psalm 105: Remember His Marvelous Works from Abraham to the Exodus

precepts.why:
“Remember his marvellous works that he hath done; his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth”. The Bible tells us to remember our past, and Paul gives the reason it was written down: “whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

The works of the Most High for our fathers were not recorded for a history lesson. They were written so that we, reading them now, might learn and have hope. That is why the psalm calls us to make known his deeds among the people, to talk of all his wondrous works and to seek his face evermore.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:

We get comfort in our afflictions from this Bible, because it is what changes us, and through the patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope. Sometimes we need affliction to get right with the Most High; in their affliction they seek him early, as Hosea 5:15 says. We need to get afflicted sometimes so we can come back to him, and the word is the comfort in it.

precepts.text: Whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

precepts.text: Whatsoever was written aforetime was written for our learning, that through patience and comfort of the scriptures we might have hope.

precepts.text: Whatsoever was written before was written for our learning, that through the scriptures we might have hope.

precepts.text: Things written before were written for our learning; nothing has changed.

Things written before were written for our learning; nothing has changed. note.label: Living a Clean Life in a Dirty World

points: For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning. So this Bible was written way before us today. This is how we go back and learn what happened in the Bible, how our forefathers dealt with certain situations. This is how we gain wisdom — from this Bible. There is nothing new under the sun, so our forefathers went through the same stuff that we did.
So when you are struggling, when your family is not listening to you, when you are at odds with your parents and your in-laws, whatever the case may be — go to the Bible, because it is in there.

That we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope. This Bible is where we are going to get patience and hope from. This is where we have got to go to get our information on how to live our life righteously and upright, with a contrite spirit. We have got to make sure our mind is set on the ultimate goal: keeping the commandments and faith in Christ. That is how we are going to make it to the kingdom, and we have got to walk as such.

Let your light so shine before men. When you come in the truth, your actions speak way more volume than your words. People have got to really see it, because a lot of us come in and they say, oh, this is a phase, he had a midlife crisis, he does not know what he wants to do in life. People really think this is a phase.

If you were in Christianity, in the church, and you said listen, I am preaching today — you would have a full house. Your family will come and support you, video camera out, oh that is my baby. But when you are talking about going out learning the laws, statutes and commandments and teaching your people, they are like, oh, that man is crazy, he crazy to go stand on the corner and teach his people repentance, he need to be in a pulpit. No. Our forefathers, even Christ, went out and taught the people. They went to the people; the people did not come to them. They were in the streets, they were in the ghettos, the slums. That is where they went to teach. They were in the worst places and they put their life on the line.

That is what we do not understand: this is a dangerous thing, us changing our life. America does not want that. Black folks changing, especially changing for God and keeping the commandments, is unheard of — it is taboo. So it makes our own people angry, and we come against each other, and we are shooting each other dead in the streets. But it happens for a reason, and we have got to get our mind right.

I am watching a series on Prime called the Underground Railroad, and I was talking about how it made me mad. But just think about it — the Most High allowed us to go through what we had to go through. He took that warrior spirit away from us so that we were in full subjection to Esau. One slave master and three hundred plus slaves, and we could not revolt, we could not bust upside his head and move on, take over or run for the border. We could not do that. We were in subjection. So our mind is screwed up. We have got to break all of that cycle out of us. It is by design, it is going to be hard, but we have got to get out there in the streets and teach.

So you coming in new in the body: learning, be patient with the people around you, be patient with yourself. Come in, learn as much as you can, apply what you can. A lot of people think, oh, I have got to know all the precepts in the bible. It would be good if you did, but everybody is not Captain Gideon — some can remember and go to and fro on every one of them, and that is a gift from God. Do not feel some type of way if you cannot, because it is all about what you apply. Knowing the scriptures is one thing, but if you do not apply them it means nothing to you, it does not profit you, because you are not even using the information that you know.

And we see that a lot. Brothers can know a million precepts, and guess what — them the first ones to bug out. He is a precept-a-con, you ask him anything and he knows exactly where it is, and then brothers be bugged out in their mind. Why? Because they do not apply it. They do not use the information that they know, so it is unprofitable to them. When we come in this truth we have got to make sure that we are not only reading the scriptures but applying them, using them.
